# Unity.Ricochet — User Stories
> ✅ done (shipped & tested) · 🟡 partial · ⬜ planned. Every ✅ cites the test.

## Priority backlog
_Nothing recorded yet._


## Epic CORE — Single-player core rebuild
- **U.RICO-US-CORE1 ⬜** As a player, I aim with an angle and power meter and see my shot's likely ricochet path off borders and redirectors before I fire, the way the 2013 original's aim/bounce-preview did.
- **U.RICO-US-CORE2 ⬜** As a host, I set up to 16 players (any mix of human and AI) with names, colours and per-player health, and play proceeds through a visible turn order with a turn timer.
- **U.RICO-US-CORE3 ⬜** As a player, I cycle through a weapon and item loadout, throw fused grenades, and pick up random weapon/item/health drops spawned on the level.
- **U.RICO-US-CORE4 ⬜** As a player, I contend with level hazards carried over from the original: a destructible shield wall, a vortex detonation, electricity and laser obstacles, and destructible borders/foliage.
- **U.RICO-US-CORE5 ⬜** As a player, I can fill empty seats with AI opponents whose count and aim-assist level I control before the match starts.
- **U.RICO-US-CORE6 ⬜** As a player, I see announcer commentary (portrait + name box) between turns and a HUD showing scores, turn time, and the current weapon/item.
- **U.RICO-US-CORE7 ⬜** As a player, I move through title, player setup, map/room select, settings, controls, how-to-play and credits screens, and see an endgame recap, matching the original's room flow.
- **U.RICO-US-CORE8 ⬜** As a player, my display name, colour and audio settings come from my MindAttic profile (Unity.Shared) instead of being re-entered every session.


## Epic NET — Real multiplayer
- **U.RICO-US-NET1 ⬜** As a player, I host a match (listen server or dedicated) or join one by IP or a short join code, through the Unity.Multiplayer drop-in front end and lobby.
- **U.RICO-US-NET2 ⬜** As a player, turn order, aiming inputs, shot resolution and damage are server-authoritative and replicated to every client, replacing the original's single-PC hotseat turn-passing.
- **U.RICO-US-NET3 ⬜** As a player who drops mid-match, my seat and health are held for the reconnect grace period and I resume on the same turn if I reconnect in time.
- **U.RICO-US-NET4 ⬜** As a player, I can start a restart or kick vote through NetVotes with the same overlay the house front end provides.


## Epic STD — Unity standards
- **U.RICO-US-STD1 ⬜** As a maintainer, every assembly is named for this game and sits behind a hard one-way boundary (Ricochet.Core <- Ricochet.Runtime <- Ricochet.Editor and tests), so nothing is still called MyGame.
- **U.RICO-US-STD2 ⬜** As a maintainer, the game's rules change state only through commands that produce events, and presentation reads state and plays the events, so a networked client, a replay and a test all drive the same path.
- **U.RICO-US-STD3 ⬜** As a designer, every tuning number and every piece of content (rules, weapons, items, maps, announcer lines, slides, names) is a data file validated on load, not a constant in behaviour.
- **U.RICO-US-STD4 ⬜** As a player, the game reads input through the Unity Input System with rebindable actions, so a controller or a rebind works and nothing depends on the legacy Input Manager.
- **U.RICO-US-STD5 ⬜** As a player, the game renders through URP with a pipeline-agnostic layer, so quality tiers and platforms work and no code names a render pipeline.
- **U.RICO-US-STD6 ⬜** As a player, the HUD and every overlay are real UI (UI Toolkit or the shared MindAttic components), so it scales, themes and sits in the right order over menus.
- **U.RICO-US-STD7 ⬜** As a maintainer, the two largest runtime classes are split into small single-purpose components, so each can be read and tested.
- **U.RICO-US-STD8 ⬜** As a maintainer, every push builds, runs the Core tests and the EditMode and PlayMode suites in CI, and the Core is covered by tests for every rule.
- **U.RICO-US-STD9 ⬜** As a reader, the README and BIBLE describe the finished game, its laws and its verified state, with nothing stale.


## Epic PAR — Parity with the original
- **U.RICO-US-PAR1 ✅** As a player, my last match setup (players, AI, skills, names, map, goal and every rule) is remembered between sessions, as the original's config.ini was.
- **U.RICO-US-PAR2 ✅** As a player, a round starts with a Ready card showing whose turn it is, a sonar ping on their tank and a short hold before the clock runs, as the original did every turn.
- **U.RICO-US-PAR3 ✅** As a player in a match, I can pause (P, Pause or the right stick; Esc stays the kit's menu) and see Resume, Randomize, Music and Quit round, as the original's pause menu offered (U.RICO-T43; `Tests/PlayMode/PauseMenuTests.cs`, `Tests/Core.Tests/PauseTests.cs`).
- **U.RICO-US-PAR4 ⬜** As a player, tanks, shots and the level are drawn with the original's art (sprites, backgrounds and fonts imported and used), not placeholder shapes.
- **U.RICO-US-PAR5 ✅** As a player, I see the original's tank: a turret that turns over a hull, and tracks left behind when it drives.
- **U.RICO-US-PAR6 ⬜** As a player, each round has its own backdrop: one of the original's 64 backgrounds in three groups, drifting clouds, soft spotlights and coloured lights.
- **U.RICO-US-PAR7 ⬜** As a player, shots look like the original's: beams, rings, swirls, fuses, electricity and glows.
- **U.RICO-US-PAR8 ⬜** As a player, hits and knock-outs have the original's effects: explosions, scorch marks, shattering glass, flying score text and falling crates with smoke.
- **U.RICO-US-PAR9 ⬜** As a player, the bottom bar shows the original's weapon and item icons with counts, tooltips, the angle readout, turn arrow and aiming guide.
- **U.RICO-US-PAR10 ✅** As a player, every action has the original's sound, not a synthesised blip.
- **U.RICO-US-PAR11 ⬜** As a player, the announcer speaks: each of the seven personalities' recorded welcome, win and lose lines play with their portrait and name box.
- **U.RICO-US-PAR12 ⬜** As a player, the title screen is the original's: the animated RICOCHET letters over its backdrop with music, then the main menu in the same style.
- **U.RICO-US-PAR13 ⬜** As a player, moving between screens fades as the original's rooms did.
- **U.RICO-US-PAR14 ⬜** As a player, the controls and how-to-play screens show the original's keyboard picture and slide images.
- **U.RICO-US-PAR15 ⬜** As a player, the credits roll over the original's credits image with its font.
- **U.RICO-US-PAR16 ⬜** As a player, the endgame shows the winners on the original's podium with confetti and the victory music.
- **U.RICO-US-PAR17 ⬜** As a player, the game opens with the original's studio splash and startup credits, in this project's own words.
- **U.RICO-US-PAR18 ⬜** As the owner, a scripted play-through of the whole game is compared screen by screen with the original, so parity is shown, not claimed.
